⊕ A little context behind the game+

Real nights. Simulated vehicles.

The replay uses historical ComEd prices. Charging behavior, vehicle state of charge, and costs are simulated; this page does not control a real charger. The day-ahead plan uses published forecasts and replans when tomorrow's prices are released at 5 p.m. Live prices appear after their seven-minute delay. In-progress bills are posted-price estimates; final bills use settled hourly prices.

Energy, with the losses included.

Energy added is the difference between the arrival battery and your selected morning target, using the modeled pack capacity. Electricity at the meter includes charging losses at an assumed 90% efficiency. Cybertruck uses an assumed 123 kWh usable pack and Model X an assumed 95 kWh usable pack; these are study assumptions, not Tesla-published usable-pack claims. Passenger charging power follows Tesla onboard charging limits.

Buses & commercial vehicles.

These options assume hourly-priced supply and compare with immediate charging on those same prices. Delivery, demand charges and infrastructure are excluded. Regular and Heavy use modeled arrival battery levels of 50% and 20%, charging to your selected morning target. The illustrative bus has a 440 kWh nominal pack and the commercial vehicle a 200 kWh nominal pack, with 90% charging efficiency. The bus pack assumption draws on published transit planning inputs. These scenarios are not measured operator maxima or winter guarantees. Fixed-rate supply alone has no energy-price timing saving.

A fair finish line.

Every strategy uses the same vehicle, arrival battery, morning target and charging window. Average (50% on arrival) and Heavy (20% on arrival) are illustrative battery presets, not measurements of an individual driver. The default 80% target is a balanced replay scenario; you can edit it from 55% to 100%. For personal vehicles, the standard-delivery immediate-charging baseline also shows the effect of changing the delivery rate. Buses and commercial vehicles compare against immediate charging on the same hourly supply prices. A lower cost only helps when the required energy is delivered by departure. A single replay is an example; use the full historical test to compare the entire set of eligible nights.

Every night has a different rhythm.
